newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen Bank postpones shareholders' meeting.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen Bank postpones shareholders' meeting.

text.p: The Shenzhen Development Bank announced on Monday that it had postponed its shareholders' meeting pending a probe into stock trading irregularities.
The stock was suspended on Monday morning for the announcement. The meeting was to have been held on Monday.
Analysts said the news was a key factor behind falls in Shenzhen stocks on Monday morning.
"People are actively selling Shenzhen-based companies' stocks after the Shenzhen Development Bank hiccuped again today," a trader at China Guotai Securities said.
The bank announced the meeting's deferral in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times. Bank officials declined to elaborate.
"This makes investors more sensitive to rumours about futher market clampdowns," the analyst said.

Beijing recently said it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading, a move seen as aimed at curbing the inflow of "hot money" into the country's stock markets, brokers said.
